President John Dramani Mahama is expected to commission new human DNA testing laboratories and a dedicated vaccine development facility at the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR) on Wednesday, November 18.
The facilities are aimed at strengthening Ghana’s capacity to conduct essential medical and scientific investigations locally and reduce dependence on foreign laboratories for the analysis of critical samples.
The Ministry of Health announced the planned commissioning in a Facebook post on Tuesday, November 17, describing the investment as an important step towards building the country’s domestic scientific and research capabilities.
According to the Ministry, recent experiences have highlighted the need for Ghana to develop the capacity to undertake critical laboratory tests within the country rather than rely on sending samples abroad for analysis.
The new laboratories are expected to improve the country’s capabilities in human DNA testing and vaccine research, while enhancing preparedness for public health emergencies.
“Tomorrow, President John Dramani Mahama will commission new DNA Laboratories for human testing, alongside a dedicated laboratory for vaccine development at the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR),” the Ministry stated.
The commissioning ceremony is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. on Wednesday at the institute in Accra.
